assessment.nobel_worthiness: GLP-1 physiology led to incretin-based drugs that transformed treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity, with large cardiovascular and metabolic benefit. A clear discovery chain from hormone biology to therapy with very broad impact on patients and on the research field.
assessment.attribution: Decisive contributions are spread: Holst on GLP-1 physiology and secretion, Drucker on GLP-1 biology and the receptor-mediated actions, Mojsov on identification and synthesis of the active peptide form, Knudsen on long-acting analogues. Habener, who is not on the supplied credit list, also seems relevant. A three-person configuration necessarily leaves out a major contributor, and the Mojsov priority question is sensitive.
assessment.maturity: Decades of clinical use and outcome trials confirm efficacy; the interpretation is stable and recognition is timely, arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Whether the prize should reward basic physiology or the therapeutic development (Knudsen's role) is unresolved.
Credit allocation among Drucker, Holst, Mojsov and Knudsen, and the omission of an uncredited early contributor, is difficult; my recollection of priority details is not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Genetically engineered T cells produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and established a new therapeutic modality. Originality, clarity and clinical impact are high.
assessment.attribution: Sadelain contributed early CAR design and costimulation, June the clinical translation and CD19 CAR-T in leukemia, Rosenberg the adoptive cell therapy framework and early clinical proof. Other early inventors such as Eshhar are not in the supplied credit list, which complicates fair allocation.
assessment.maturity: Several approved products and long follow-up show durable responses in some patients; solid-tumor results and toxicity remain limited, but the core discovery is mature enough.
uncertainties: Credit for the original chimeric receptor concept falls outside the supplied names.
Long-term safety, including secondary malignancy signals, is still being defined.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response revealed a new intracellular signalling logic from the ER to the nucleus, with consequences for secretion, metabolism, neurodegeneration and cancer. An original, clear and conceptually fundamental discovery with a long record of consequence.
assessment.attribution: Walter and Mori are the two people most associated with the decisive mechanistic work: Mori the transcriptional response and Hac1/Ire1 pathway genetics, Walter the Ire1 kinase/RNase and splicing mechanism. A two-person prize is natural; I recognise Ron and others as relevant but they are not on the supplied credit list.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism confirmed independently over three decades in yeast and mammals; recognition is timely. Direct therapeutic translation is still developing.
uncertainties: Medical impact is more indirect than for therapeutic discoveries.
The roles of other contributors cannot be assessed from the supplied credit list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Light-gated channels enabled cell-type-specific control of activity in intact tissue, transforming experimental neuroscience and physiology, with growing translational reach. Technical originality and field impact are substantial.
assessment.attribution: Channelrhodopsin identification and characterisation (Nagel, Hegemann, Bamberg) and its adaptation to neurons and behaviour (Boyden, Deisseroth, with Miesenböck's earlier genetic photostimulation) make this a six-plus-person candidate; a three-person split leaves out others and requires a judgment between discovery and application.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and used for two decades; clinical use is only beginning (vision restoration), so the prize case rests on research tool impact.
uncertainties: Unresolved credit between protein discoverers and neuroscience applicators.
Whether a tool and technology of this kind fits best within this prize is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: L1 virus-like particle vaccines prevent persistent HPV infection and precancer, with national-programme data now showing near elimination of cervical disease in vaccinated cohorts. Major public-health consequence building on a previously recognised link between HPV and cervical cancer.
assessment.attribution: Lowy and Schiller developed the papillomavirus VLP platform and its immunogenicity; Frazer made key contributions including early VLP work with Zhou, who died in 1999 and is not in the supplied list. Credit disputes among groups, including Georgetown and Rochester work, exist.
assessment.maturity: Population-level effectiveness data over more than a decade support the claim; recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Priority among several groups developing VLPs is contested.
Part of the field's recognition already went to the HPV-cancer discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Imatinib validated the rational targeting of an oncogenic kinase, converting CML from a fatal to a chronic condition, and made the paradigm of targeted cancer therapy. The impact is clear and lasting.
assessment.attribution: Lydon led the compound program, Druker the clinical translation, Sawyers the resistance work and second-generation inhibitors. Rowley's and Witte's earlier BCR-ABL discoveries are outside the supplied credit set. This is a reasonable three-person configuration for the therapeutic step.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of survival data; very mature and, if anything, a late recognition candidate.
uncertainties: Possible concern that the foundational Philadelphia chromosome and BCR-ABL discoveries are separate, partly pre-credited steps.
Prior major awards raise questions of whether a prize adds distinct recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR, discovered through rapamycin's mode of action, defines a central growth-control and nutrient-sensing pathway with implications for cancer, metabolism, ageing and immunosuppression. Fundamental and wide-reaching.
assessment.attribution: Hall identified TOR genetically in yeast and established its role in growth control; Schreiber's group's work on FKBP-rapamycin and the mammalian target was important. Sabatini's contributions to mTORC1 regulation are credited but I avoid including him because of unresolved questions on subsequent allocation and conduct that I cannot verify here.
assessment.maturity: Highly confirmed across organisms; clinical use of rapalogs is established, though the broader therapeutic promise for ageing is not proven.
uncertainties: Allocation among Hall, Schreiber, Sabatini and others is not clean.
Rapamycin's own discovery (Sehgal, Vezina) is outside the supplied credit set.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Antisense correction of SMN2 splicing produced nusinersen, a disease-modifying therapy for spinal muscular atrophy, and showed the clinical value of splice-modulating oligonucleotides for a severe genetic disease. A clear gene-to-therapy chain.
assessment.attribution: Krainer provided the splicing mechanism and the ASO target concept, Bennett the chemistry and development at Ibis/Isis. The two-person configuration is sensible; other developers of SMN biology such as Melki, Lefebvre and Dreyfuss are not in the supplied credit list.
assessment.maturity: Approved in 2016 with years of long-term data, though the field of oligonucleotide medicine is still evolving, so some may view it as premature relative to the older discoveries above.
uncertainties: Whether the underlying SMN gene discovery should be recognised alongside the therapy is unresolved.
Recognition may be early compared with candidates with longer follow-up.
